rationale: Frozen protocol for the weekly open-weight model wave (founder directive 2026-10-13; docs/META_REVIEW_2026-10-13_ITER97-101.md sections 5 and 6, R1 and R2). Every value below is held fixed across waves so that a wave may change only its new subjects. weekly-wave.mjs generates each wave's run-config.json and PREREGISTRATION.md from this file plus QUEUE.json, and refuses (check, collect) any run-config that differs from it in a fixed field. Changing this file is a versioned, founder-approved event: bump protocol_version, never edit a field in place for one week. Code treats only status 'ratified' as usable for a real plan; the founder ratifies by changing status to 'ratified' and committing. Values are carried over from pilot-2026-10-03 (bank, judges, batch size, validity rule, system message, trials). The reference build is re-run in every wave as an in-wave comparator and, across weeks, as an instrument-stability series: the same digest-pinned build should keep scoring about the same, and a drift in its composite points at the judging or the host, not at the model. Known cost: gemma2:9b loads at about 7.1 GB and does not fit an 8 GB GPU entirely (pilot-2026-10-03 deviation D1), so about 20% of it runs from system RAM; collect checks free memory before it starts.

reference.label: gemma2-9b-A
reference.note: In-wave comparator, re-run every week at 1 trial (83 calls). Its composite across weeks is also an instrument-stability series.

anchor.rationale: Each wave has judges re-rate a seeded sample of stored pilot-2026-10-03 replies (6 per source subject) and reports the mean absolute difference from the original rating. The only observation so far is the pilot-2026-10-03 bridge against pilot-2026-10-02: mean 0.146, 41 of 48 rating pairs exact. The threshold 0.30 is about twice that observation, so ordinary session-to-session noise passes and a clear shift in judging is flagged. A wave whose mean absolute difference is above the threshold is marked 'not comparable'. It is a starting value and the founder may revise it only by a new protocol version, with the drift series available as evidence.

size_unit: GB means 1e9 bytes (Ollama /api/tags size field divided by 1e9)

comparisons.rule: Every subject in a wave uses arm A. Comparisons are each new subject against the reference, then each pair of new subjects. All are kind 'build'. checkConformance requires exactly this generated set.
